topic.title: Promptable Segmentation and Learning from Weak Visual Supervision
topic.overview: Segmentation assigns pixels to meaningful objects or regions. This cluster focuses on reducing annotation requirements and making segmentation responsive to prompts, language, and broader visual understanding. One unsupervised approach builds hierarchical masks by combining top-down image partitioning with bottom-up merging, then uses those masks to train a promptable segmentation model.
topic.whyItMatters: Dense human labels are expensive and may omit objects outside an annotation scheme. Weak supervision, automatically discovered masks, and synthetic scenes can widen coverage, but their usefulness depends on spatial detail and the quality of object boundaries.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with partially labeled images and structured scene parsing. Later work develops object candidates and general-purpose segmentation. Recent papers explore unsupervised multi-object discovery, language prompts, generative segmentation, and which properties of synthetic images improve dense visual representations.
openQuestions: How can automatically generated masks be checked without recreating a full labeling effort?
Which synthetic scene properties transfer reliably to unfamiliar real-world imagery?
